questions.question: In the two-stage architecture, why does the recall stage use a bi-encoder rather than a cross-encoder?
options: A bi-encoder is more accurate and ranks the true order in one pass
A bi-encoder can precompute document vectors offline so only the query is encoded online — fast enough to fish candidates out of a hundred thousand chunks
A bi-encoder does not need an embedding model
questions.explanation: See the "The two-stage architecture: not missing, not misordering" section: the bi-encoder can precompute document vectors offline and encode one query online, fishing a top-50/top-10 out of a hundred thousand chunks in milliseconds — its mandate is "not missing".

questions.question: For the "cross-city return shipping" question, why can the cross-encoder spot the answer chunk while the bi-encoder misses it?
options: The answer chunk has higher vector dimensions
It matches "cross-city" with "different-region" — a synonym swap that surfaces in word-level interaction, with lexical overlap too thin for the two towers to see
The bi-encoder's similarity threshold was set too low
The cross-encoder retrains the document vectors
questions.explanation: See the "cross-encoder versus bi-encoder" section: it matches "cross-city" with "different-region", lexical overlap too thin for the two towers to see, and the cross-encoder catches it at a glance.

questions.question: "The top 3 decide the answer quality" is the joint conclusion of the prompt budget and which effect?
options: Position bias — LLMs attend more to, and trust more, context placed earlier
questions.explanation: See the "Rescoring and the top-3 effect" section: one, seats — the window budget is finite; two, position bias — LLMs attend more to, and trust more, context placed earlier.
